  "summary": "These minutes record the All India Swatantra Party National Executive’s meeting held in Bombay on 29 June 1976, with the document issued from the party’s Madras headquarters on 4 September 1976. The Executive rejected the ruling party’s proposed constitutional amendments, except those concerning territorial matters, arguing that India’s economic difficulties resulted from poor governance and economic mismanagement rather than defects in the Constitution. It reaffirmed support for the Constitution in its original form and assigned General Secretary Girish Munshi to prepare comments on the Swaran Singh Committee report and Jayaprakash Narayan’s committee report.\n\nThe minutes also address the proposed formation of a new opposition party under Jayaprakash Narayan. Swatantra welcomed efforts to create a viable democratic, non-communist alternative but withheld full approval because it objected to several economic proposals and because the proposed arrangement did not ensure that existing parties would dissolve. The Executive connected free elections to the withdrawal of the Emergency, restoration of fundamental rights and freedoms, and the removal of press censorship, warning that elections under the prevailing conditions would be fraudulent. It concluded by authorising small-group party discussions and noting that an alternative Janata Party draft received from the BLD broadly accorded with Swatantra’s position.",
